attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter. The quoted Bloomberg passage nearby is separate and not part of this claim.

semantics.note: This is a firm judgment that more than $100B a year exceeds what private credit funds would take on. The drafter's 'unlikely' modality label is not in the source, but the wording itself is unhedged. The margin and competition remarks are reasons, not conditions.

contract.note: Reading 'could stomach' as the funds not supplying more than $100B to OpenAI within any twelve-month window is an ordinary plain reading. Correctly, no early support can come from deals not happening, given there is no endpoint.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's own disclosure about broad platforms to mobilise financing. It shows no private credit money actually supplied to OpenAI.

reviews.rationale: 'Foreseeable future' sets no deadline, and the first twelve-month window after the August 2026 post has not ended. The packet shows no private credit financing to OpenAI above $100B, and no ledger of payouts. The only evidence is NVIDIA context. The forecast can be neither confirmed nor refuted yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence, within his scenario of OpenAI being allowed to run out of money.

semantics.note: The consequent is firm ('will'), inside the scenario of OpenAI failing. The antecedent is kept. The 70% figure is an embedded historical premise, and the blame clause is reasonably left out.

contract.note: Treating OpenAI's 'death' as stopping operations and compute payments matches the scenario. Allowing for replacement demand in judging a material revenue loss is fair.

evidence.note: Google Cloud's own announcement, dated 21 Oct 2026, of launching OpenAI models. It shows OpenAI still operating, so the antecedent is unmet. It says nothing about the consequent.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast whose antecedent, OpenAI failing, has not happened: the evidence shows OpenAI still trading commercially in October 2026. Under the policy an unmet conditional is not scored. No deadline was given, and the 70% premise was not verified from readable filings.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his analysis of OpenAI's obligations.

semantics.note: The claim is that much of the money comes due by end-2027, which will require at least one more massive funding round. Firm 'will'. The horizon and the 'at least one' quantifier are kept.

contract.note: Requiring a separate new round after publication, a substantial share falling due, and real financial need is a fair reading. Opportunistic fundraising alone would not count.

evidence.note: Bloomberg report of 23 Oct 2026 that new fundraising talks are ongoing. It shows negotiations, not a completed round or a proven funding gap.

reviews.rationale: The deadline is 31 Dec 2027, after the evaluation date. The evidence shows only ongoing talks, not a completed new round tied to obligations falling due, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Not yet scoreable.

semantics.note: A compound present-tense observation: over $300B in commitments due within three years, and Anthropic similarly unprofitable to OpenAI. The revised wording keeps 'similarly' rather than claiming equal losses.

contract.note: Reading 'due in the next three years' as payable by Aug 2029, and 'similarly unprofitable' as both being loss-making, is ordinary. Net versus operating profit is a real ambiguity, and it is flagged.

evidence.note: S-1 shows about $321.4B in leases not yet commenced at 30 June 2026, with terms up to 20 years. Not all of it falls due within three years, so the three-year total is not established either way.
Reports a Q2 2026 net loss of $66.3B but a first operating profit. Whether Anthropic counts as unprofitable depends on the measure, and there is no matched OpenAI figure.

reviews.rationale: The filing shows large commitments but no schedule of amounts payable by Aug 2029, so the over-$300B three-year claim is unsettled. Anthropic had a Q2 net loss but an operating profit, and the packet has no comparable OpenAI results. Neither part is established or refuted.
